Implemented a385316_census_v3.py — a numpy-based two-pass census enumerator for unordered prime-cube triplets (p≤q≤r) with p³+q³+r³ ≤ C. Wrote experiment.json with filled hypothesis. Ran verification at C=10⁷ and confirmed a(1)=24 and a(2)=185527 with representations [(13,43,47)] and [(19,31,53)]. The verification of a(3)–a(5) failed because the assumed OEIS terms (159067, 229219, 499806) do not match the actual enumeration — smallest multiplicity-3 is ≥500000 (outside C=10⁷), and multiplicity-4/5 may not appear until much higher. The census script itself (pass 1: enumerate, pass 2: numpy sort + diff runlength) is correct; the bug was in the verification fixture data, not the enumeration logic.
